title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed 1 day (1/7) in a 7-day week; historical sales during closures show ~14% drop in comparable weeks (e.g., 2026-09-28: 24 units vs baseline 44.1, 2.3% price increase, but closure not noted; 2026-08-31: 43 units, no closure, similar baseline).

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Past 10% off promotions lifted sales x1.25 (noise-adjusted), implying ~25% demand elasticity. A 2.3% price rise likely reduces demand ~15%. Two recent weeks at $6.56 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) sold at 54% and 53% of baseline, respectively.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 44.1 is adjusted downward due to the store closure on Monday (1/7 of week lost), reducing expected sales. The price increase to $6.56 (+2.3%) likely suppresses demand, with past 10% off promotions averaging x1.25 noise-adjusted lift, suggesting a price-sensitive product. A 2.3% increase implies a likely ~15% demand drop (consistent with past price sensitivity). The closure and price rise act as independent downward drivers. No promotion or event is scheduled, and the classical model suggests no uplift, which is credible given the lack of historical promotion in this period. Evidence for price effect is moderate (2 past weeks at $6.56 with lower sales). Combined, the median is reduced. Spreads remain unchanged as the uncertainty is not higher than baseline.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.1 | 5%-95%: 10.5 - 75.8 | 10%-90%: 19.4 - 71.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
